00024106d6d87a8d.title: Teaching AI Agent to Play Poker Strategically Through Preference Optimization
00024106d6d87a8d.title_original: Teaching AI Agent to Play Poker Strategically Through Preference Optimization
00024106d6d87a8d.summary: arXiv:2610.27028v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A poker agent can make a legal move and still make a strategically poor one. We ask whether compact AI agents can exhibit strategic behavior under hidden information and whether preference optimization can improve beyond static and zero-shot policies. We first evaluate a static baseline and three frozen language models: SmallThinker, Qwen3, and Gemma-3 whose performance varies substantially between exact-game and six-player evaluation. We therefore propose Strategic Preference Optimization with KL-anchored Equilibrium (SPOKE), combining teacher-relative value penalties, policy anchoring, risk constraints, and structured rationale supervision, and compare it with SFT, DPO, GRPO, and GSPO. Across three runs of a SmallThinker-4B-A0.6B policy, SPOKE achieves the lowest mean exploitability in Kuhn (0.213) and Leduc (1.081) and the highest six-max top-1 agreement (0.775), while maintaining teacher KL comparable to SFT (0.522 vs 0.523). These results provide preliminary evidence that strategic preference optimization can improve strategic quality while preserving teacher-consistent behavior.

582b3357edf1be20.title: Repair, Retry, and the Cost of Hindsight: Verifier Feedback in Formal Theorem Proving
582b3357edf1be20.title_original: Repair, Retry, and the Cost of Hindsight: Verifier Feedback in Formal Theorem Proving
582b3357edf1be20.summary: arXiv:2610.22698v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Verifier-guided self-repair conditions a model on feedback from failed attempts before it tries again, without weight updates. Yet two findings in prior work are in tension: verifier feedback can improve repair of failures, but self-repair itself can provide little-to-no advantage over independent resampling. We reconcile these findings in Lean theorem proving through controlled one-step experiments that hold the preceding failure fixed while varying whether the failed proof is shown, whether the compiler error corresponds to that failure, and the retry instruction. We test frozen Qwen3.6-27B, a general-purpose model, and DeepSeek-Prover-V2-7B, a specialized prover, on difficult MiniF2F problems. We find two opposing effects. Showing the model its failed predecessor reduces success and sharply increases copying of it, while on Qwen adding that attempt's compiler error recovers the loss, to the level of the diagnostic alone. Replacing the predecessor with another theorem's failed proof largely removes the degradation on both models; on Qwen, replacing the diagnostic with another problem's error substantially reduces the recovery. Without the failed proof, correct diagnostics show no resolved advantage over wrong-diagnostic controls on either model. The failed-proof penalty persists with and without the retry instruction, whereas Qwen's diagnostic recovery is weaker without it. In 11-problem sequential experiments through 64 attempts, Qwen retains a correct-diagnostic benefit within failed-proof histories, while DeepSeek-Prover shows no resolved recovery. However, no tested one-step feedback condition establishes an advantage over instruction-only resampling, nor does 64-attempt sequential repair with failed proofs and correct diagnostics at equal token budgets. Verifier feedback can thus improve repair without overcoming the performance loss from conditioning on a failed attempt.

401856f016d5ae46.title_original: 雷神 ZERO Air 15 双十一开启优惠：1.54kg 轻量机身搭载 RTX 5060，支持 160W 性能释放
401856f016d5ae46.summary: IT之家 10 月 14 日消息，双十一大促已经开启，笔记本市场也迎来集中优惠。 对于不少用户来说，如今一台电脑的使用场景已经不再局限于单纯游戏，日常办公、内容创作、影音娱乐等需求也越来越常见。因此，在选择游戏本时，除了关注处理器和显卡性能，机身重量、屏幕体验以及移动便携性也成为不少消费者考虑的因素。 此前在 CES 2026 上，雷神推出了全新的 LightGaming 轻型游戏本产品 —— 雷神 ZERO Air 15。该产品主打在轻量化机身中实现较高性能释放，官方数据显示，其整机重量约 1.54kg，厚度薄至 15.9mm，同时支持最高 160W 性能输出。双十一期间，雷神 ZERO Air 15 国补后售价为 12449 元。 在设计方面，雷神 ZERO Air 15 采用轻量化机身方案。机身外壳选用航空级镁合金材质，并通过结构优化降低整机重量，同时提升机身强度。此外，该机还采用定制轻量化主板，并对内部散热结构进行调整，通过 VC 架构散热方案进一步优化空间利用。 外观方面，机器表面采用准分子 UV 肤感漆工艺，通过多道工序处理后呈现哑光质感，同时具备一定抗指纹能力。对于需要经常携带电脑外出的用户来说，1.54kg 的重量相比传统游戏本更方便放入背包，减少移动负担。 性能方面，雷神 ZERO Air 15 搭载第三代英特尔酷睿 Ultra 7 356H 处理器，采用 16 核 16 线程设计，最高睿频可达 4.7GHz，并内置 NPU，可支持 AI 相关应用。 显卡方面，该机配备 NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5060 Laptop GPU，基于 Blackwell 架构打造，拥有 8GB GDDR7 显存，支持 115W 满功耗释放，提供 3328 个 CUDA 核心以及 572TOPS AI 算力，同时支持 DLSS 5 和 Max-Q 技术。 雷神 ZERO Air 15 搭载 Aero 真空腔散热系统，通过 VC 真空腔均热板、定制风扇以及相变硅脂等组件优化散热效率。官方数据显示，该机 CPU+GPU 双平台最高可实现 160W 性能释放，轻松满足游戏以及部分创作场景需求。 屏幕方面，雷神 ZERO Air 15 配备 15.3 英寸 OLED 屏幕，分辨率为 2560×1600，刷新率达到 165Hz，并支持 100% DCI-P3 色域、10bit 色深以及 HDR 显示，经过出厂校色。 存储配置方面，机器搭载 32GB DDR5 内存和 1TB SSD，同时提供双 SO-DIMM 内存插槽以及双 M.2 硬盘位，方便用户后续升级。显示模式方面，设备支持独显直连、混合输出以及核显输出三种模式切换，可以根据游戏性能需求和日常续航需求进行调整。 其他配置方面，雷神 ZERO Air 15 配备全尺寸 RGB 背光键盘、独立数字小键盘以及类玻璃触控板，同时搭载带物理遮挡开关的摄像头，提升隐私保护能力。接口方面提供 RJ45 网口、USB-A、USB-C 等接口，并搭配 250W 轻量化 SiC 电源适配器，方便日常携带。 双十一期间，雷神 ZERO Air 15 国补后售价为 12449 元，并提供雷神休闲背包、加速器季卡以及 Microsoft 365 个人版三个月订阅等购机权益。 京东 雷神 ZEROAir 15“小轻龙”游戏笔记本电脑 （英特尔酷睿 Ultra 7 356H RTX5060 32G 1T OLED 黑）国家补贴 国补后 12449 元起 直达链接 京东 11.11 无门槛红包 面额至高 26888 元，每天抽 3 次： 点此抽红包 。

3d847813d5ed14c1.title: 消息称华为乾崑准备推出新智驾方案：比 ADS Pro 更便宜，但又高于 SE 版本
3d847813d5ed14c1.title_original: 消息称华为乾崑准备推出新智驾方案：比 ADS Pro 更便宜，但又高于 SE 版本
3d847813d5ed14c1.summary: IT之家 10 月 20 日消息，据博主 @新出行贺磊 分享， 华为乾崑最近的智驾用户开通费的问题开始遇到阻力 ，他们也在积极地调研中。 该博主透露，华为乾崑准备推出一款新的智驾方案， 价格比 ADS Pro 更便宜，但又高于 SE 版本 。博主还在评论区补充， 称新方案对比的是 SE，应该能力是提升的 。 据IT之家了解，华为乾崑智驾共有 Ultra / Max / Pro / SE 四个档位： 第 1 档是 ADS SE 基础版：满足基本的主动安全、泊车辅助、高速 NCA 及城区 LCC+ 功能，经济型车型首选。 第 2 档是 ADS Pro 增强版：搭载舱内激光视觉传感器，主动安全能力与城区 LCC+ 功能进一步增强，标准型车型首选。 第 3 档是 ADS Max 超阶版：搭载高性能超远距激光，可选配分布式毫米波雷达及高精度固态激光雷达，支持全维主动安全、高速 NCA、城区 NCA 及车位到车位与泊车代驾等高级功能，豪华型车型首选。 第 4 档是 ADS Ultra 旗舰版：具备高速 L3 能力，高端旗舰车型首选。 在今年 4 月 23 日晚，华为乾崑智驾 ADS 5 正式发布 。算法层面，华为发布了面向自动驾驶的 AI 智能体 WEWA 2.0 架构。该架构在云端引入 Multi-Agent 博弈技术与在线强化学习机制；在车端应用了安全风险场技术进行实时安全评估，并通过 Driving Agent 模块完成出行任务的策略优化。 华为官方曾表示，华为乾崑智驾 ADS 4 Max / Pro / SE 升级到华为乾崑智驾 ADS 5 Max / Pro / SE 对应版本，不存在硬件限制。 今年 6 月，华为乾崑智驾 ADS Max 高阶功能包限时优惠价格到期，自 7 月 1 日起将恢复原标准价格（一次性购买 36000 元）。不过车企一般会推出智驾功能包的优惠活动， 搭载舱内激光雷达的 Pro 方案首月价格 6,000 元、搭载 896 线双光路图像级激光雷达的 Max 到 Ultra 方案首月价格 15,000 元 。 ▲ 图源：华为乾崑智能汽车解决方案官网

7e1fa4f2506d36fb.title: 首张全天紫外线地图问世：Claude Science AI 协助绘制约 1/3 区域
7e1fa4f2506d36fb.title_original: 首张全天紫外线地图问世：Claude Science AI 协助绘制约 1/3 区域
7e1fa4f2506d36fb.summary: IT之家 10 月 10 日消息，Anthropic 于 10 月 8 日发布博文， 宣布旗下 Claude Science 协助绘制首张完整的全天紫外线地图，约三分之一地图区域由模型估算。 IT之家注：完整全天紫外线地图是把整片天空的紫外线观测拼合成一张图，图中以银河系中心为中央，合并了远紫外线（154 纳米）与近紫外线（232 纳米）数据。 由于地球臭氧层会吸收紫外线，因此天文学家必须使用太空望远镜观测。其中最大的数据集来自 NASA 的 GALEX 任务，在 2003 至 2013 年间拍摄约 3.8 万次，覆盖约三分之二天空。而为了保护探测器，避开部分明亮恒星密集区域，剩余三分之一天空此前没有紫外线观测。 研究团队整合 GALEX、NASA Swift、韩国 FIMS / SPEAR 等任务的数据，并校准不同仪器的观测、统一分辨率与坐标。对于没有紫外线观测的区域，Claude Science 根据已有区域中紫外线亮度与可见光、红外线、射电数据的关系，估算缺失部分。 天空的三种视角：可见光、红外线和射电波段。图片来源：ESA Gaia DR3、NASA WISE、HI4PI。 因此，这张图并非每个像素都来自紫外线实测，约三分之一，包括银河系盘面的大片区域，是模型估算的。图层还标注像素属于“实测”或“预测”，并提供估算不确定度。

9a2749e5a82244b9.title: Manus：正组建团队开发面向国内市场的产品，与国产模型厂商合作稳步进行中
9a2749e5a82244b9.title_original: Manus：正组建团队开发面向国内市场的产品，与国产模型厂商合作稳步进行中
9a2749e5a82244b9.summary: IT之家 9 月 28 日消息，北京蝴蝶效应科技有限公司公众号今日发文，宣布面向海外用户发布 Manus 2.0 版本，并推出面向个人生活场景的智能助理 Cue。 Manus 表示，公司正在组建团队开发面向国内市场的产品，与国产模型厂商及生态伙伴的合作也在稳步进行，后续将分享更多进展。 IT之家注：Cue 被定位为面向个人生活场景的智能助理，Manus 2.0 面向海外用户发布，国内版本仍在筹备中。 Manus 2.0 已在网页端、桌面端和移动端上线，Cue 同步上线，iOS 版本将在通过 App Store 审核后推出。 据介绍，Manus 2.0 采用自研 Agent 框架 Cascade。官方称，该框架让项目保持轻量，仅在需要时引入专业能力。在一项测试配置中，Cascade 的 Token 消耗减少 23.2%，任务完成时间缩短 28.2%，运行成本降低 32%。 云电脑功能允许用户购买专属运行环境，用于多人游戏服务器或长期运行的自动化流程。项目可在用户合上笔记本后继续在线运行。 自动化能力从定时任务扩展至事件触发。新邮件、广告数据波动、日历事件、Slack 消息、Notion 更新等，均可触发 Manus 执行预设工作流。 桌面应用升级为 Manus Studio，定位为人与 AI 共享的工作空间。Studio 按项目需要引入能力，本次升级覆盖文档、表格、PDF、幻灯片、网站、代码、游戏和视频。 视频编辑器可生成初剪版本，并将时间线交给用户。片段、图片、文字、动态图形和音频以独立素材呈现，用户可替换配乐、素材和动画，也可交还 Manus 继续修改。 该编辑器面向 30 至 60 秒短篇产品广告、AI UGC、数据动态图表、教程、Vlog 及动效视频。Alchemy 模式由 Manus 接手创意指导，调用视频生成与代码生成能力。 游戏开发环境调用视频、图像和编程模型。Max Ultra 模式下，官方称游戏画面、玩法和手感有所提升。用户可从模板起步，在编辑面板中管理素材、修改代码和调整场景。 游戏完成后可发布为网站，也可配置多人联机。用户选择云电脑并购买后，Manus 负责托管、网络和运维。竞速、对战、竞技和 3D 游戏均支持多人联机。 远程控制与 Computer Use 功能允许用户通过 Manus 操作远程电脑。在已授权会话中，Manus 在独立可见的工作区操作，仅使用用户批准的文件、浏览器和应用。 Cue 是一款独立应用，支持手机和桌面，与 Manus 基于同一套基础设施构建。每个 Agent 拥有自己的邮箱、电话号码、钱包和电脑，可发消息、在预算内付款并完成任务。 多个 Agent 可加入同一群聊，围绕共同目标互相接力，分别负责调研、整理名单和起草文稿。Cue 还可对接日常服务，例如在餐厅扫码后由 Agent 点餐或排队取号。 Cue 目前处于抢先体验阶段，凭邀请码免费使用。官方提供邀请码 MEETCUE（限前 1000 位用户）。获得体验资格的用户还将收到可分享给他人的邀请码。

745fce089ec4b6b2.title: “我们不是美国”：澳大利亚政界商界称民众抵制 AI 数据中心是受美国舆论影响
745fce089ec4b6b2.title_original: “我们不是美国”：澳大利亚政界商界称民众抵制 AI 数据中心是受美国舆论影响
745fce089ec4b6b2.summary: IT之家 9 月 27 日消息，据卫报报道，澳大利亚政界和商界人士认为，当地民众对 AI 数据中心日益增长的不满情绪，很大程度上是从美国“输入”而来的，并不能完全反映澳大利亚本土的实际情况。 IT之家注意到，与美国类似，随着大规模 AI 数据中心建设加速，澳大利亚一些社区对这类项目的抵触情绪也在不断增加。不过，支持数据中心建设的政府官员和企业高管认为，澳大利亚的数据中心建设规模更小，监管也更加严格，因此对当地环境和社会造成的影响远低于美国。他们表示，美国国内围绕数据中心展开的激烈争论，通过社交媒体传播到澳大利亚，正在加剧当地的负面情绪。 去年美国开始出现针对数据中心的大规模反对浪潮时，这股情绪在澳大利亚还比较有限。但到了 2026 年，相关争议已经迅速演变成全国性话题，并引发了要求暂停全国数据中心建设的呼声、社区抗议活动以及 3 项政府调查。与此同时，澳大利亚各州正在制定相关框架，联邦政府也开始着手制定数据中心建设以及能源、水资源使用方面的规则。 澳大利亚各州政府都在寻求经济增长，因此总体上对新数据中心带来的投资持欢迎态度。有些项目规模巨大，甚至促使州政府绕过地方议会原本的审批流程。 今年 7 月，时任维多利亚州经济增长部长史蒂夫 · 迪莫普洛斯（Steve Dimopoulos）曾表示，从数据中心数量来看，维多利亚州仅次于新南威尔士州，而且新数据中心的增长速度已经超过澳大利亚人口最多的新南威尔士州。他表示，民众对新开发项目的不满情绪日益高涨，这是受美国社交媒体影响的结果。 他说：“我们看到美国一些州正在考虑禁止新的大型数据中心，而美国当地的相关运动以及大型项目正在影响澳大利亚的公众舆论。因为当这些内容出现在你的手机上时，你会觉得它就在身边，或者认为类似情况可能很快就会来到这里。” 这位部长还表示：“我们不是美国。我们的规划、能源和水资源体系受到更加严格的监测、管理和监管。” 数据中心行业的负责人同样对这股反弹情绪表示不满，认为相关讨论存在误导性，而且缺乏事实依据。 数据中心行业主要游说组织 Data Centres Australia 负责人贝琳达 · 丹尼特（Belinda Dennett）今年 3 月在一次演讲中表示：“澳大利亚的数据中心争论，是建立在美国数据基础上的。” 丹尼特称，普通民众对数据中心的反应从好奇、困惑到恐惧不等，而媒体对这一行业的报道“令人担忧”。她说：“这个行业被描述成能源吸血鬼、用水大户和就业杀手。问题在于，其中大多数新闻标题都源自美国，而美国的数据中心行业规模完全不同，所处的市场规则也完全不同。这些说法被原封不动地移植到澳大利亚的讨论中，仿佛两国的情况完全可以相互比较。” 丹尼特表示，美国拥有 5400 座数据中心，总容量达到 53.7GW；相比之下，澳大利亚拥有 252 座数据中心，总容量为 1.4GW。不过，美国数据中心数量的统计结果在不同来源之间存在差异。 她说：“当人们看到数据中心给电网带来压力、推高电费并消耗大量水资源的报道时，他们看到的是美国面临的问题，却未经分析就将这些问题套用到了澳大利亚市场，而两者几乎没有可比性。” 不过，丹尼特没有提到的是，澳大利亚人口约 2800 万，目前平均每 10 万人拥有不到 1 座数据中心；美国人口约 3.427 亿，平均每 10 万人拥有约 1.5 座数据中心。 与此同时，澳大利亚的数据中心建设正在迅速提速。目前已有多个容量达到 1GW 甚至更高的大型数据中心处于规划阶段。 TikTok 和 Instagram 上的热门视频也开始集中讨论当地社区对这些项目的担忧，其中包括计划建设在墨尔本外围、容量达到 2.4GW 的数据中心，以及位于北领地、计划采用燃气供电、容量达到 2GW 的数据中心。 悉尼大学数字政策教授兼高级研究员罗布 · 尼科尔斯（Rob Nicholls）表示，2GW 相当于约 200 万户家庭一年的用电量。而北领地总人口仅略高于 26.5 万人。 澳大利亚政府注意到了美国因数据中心电力需求增长而带动天然气行业扩张的情况，因此计划绕过州政府权限，禁止使用天然气为数据中心供电。 根据拟议的新规则，数据中心运营商必须向电力系统新增相当于其自身用电量的可再生能源供应。 不过，也有一些专家认为，澳大利亚民众参考美国的情况对数据中心提出质疑是合理的。 尼科尔斯表示：“来自美国社交媒体的声音非常强烈，而且背后有合理的逻辑：‘它会提高电价，也会提高水价，而我得不到任何好处。’这是一种合理的立场。” 尼科尔斯认为，澳大利亚政府面临的难题，是向民众解释美国所面对的问题与澳大利亚当地的问题究竟存在怎样的差异。 相关监管框架的立法工作预计要到明年才会推进，这也促使一些人呼吁澳大利亚效仿纽约州，在正式规则出台之前暂停新的数据中心项目。 在此之前，澳大利亚目前已经有两项州级调查和一项联邦调查正在审查数据中心行业，同时新的项目申请仍在不断增加，并持续引发当地居民的反对。 澳大利亚许多数据中心由美国企业所有。澳大利亚联邦政府技术助理部长安德鲁 · 查尔顿（Andrew Charlton）表示，由于运营这些设施的许多企业并非澳大利亚公司，当地民众可能因此对数据中心项目持怀疑态度。 微软和亚马逊已经运营多个数据中心，而 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 也正在考虑在澳大利亚建设自己的数据中心。 查尔顿本周在一次演讲中表示：“仅仅在澳大利亚建设数据中心，并不意味着澳大利亚就能获得 AI 产业带来的经济利益。我们可以提供土地，可以提供电力，可以托管这些机器，但最终仍可能发现，大部分价值以及大量经济收益都流向了海外。” 查尔顿呼吁，希望在澳大利亚建设数据中心的企业能够以优惠条件，为澳大利亚初创企业、研究人员和非营利组织提供计算资源。他还提出，澳大利亚可以基于开放权重模型打造本土 AI 能力。 查尔顿警告称：“我们可能最终会变得依赖进口的智能本身。”

6a9fb138de57c69a.title: $M^3$: A Multi-LLM System for Multi-Turn Jailbreaking as a Markov Decision Process
6a9fb138de57c69a.title_original: $M^3$: A Multi-LLM System for Multi-Turn Jailbreaking as a Markov Decision Process
6a9fb138de57c69a.summary: arXiv:2610.31937v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Modern Large Language Models (LLMs) remain vulnerable to carefully orchestrated multi-turn interactions that progressively bypass safety mechanisms. However, many existing red-teaming approaches rely on heuristics or impose strong assumptions that limit their applicability in fully black box settings. We address this gap by introducing $M^3$, an automated red-teaming framework that formalizes multi-turn jailbreaking as a finite-horizon Markov Decision Process (MDP). In $M^3$, an attacker LLM interacts with a target LLM while operating over a compact internal state produced by a state LLM. Across two benchmarks and six target models, $M^3$ consistently outperforms state-of-the-art multi-turn red-teaming methods in Attack Success Rates (ASR), achieving improvements of up to 53% in ASR@5. Even with lightweight attacker, $M^3$ attains gains up to 26% in ASR@1 and 34% in ASR@5, compared to baselines that use higher capacity attackers. Beyond improved effectiveness, $M^3$ exhibits steeper risk escalation over conversational turns and achieves more consistent performance across risk categories (up to 4.82 improvement in Gini index) without relying on predefined risk taxonomy, providing a scalable and principled framework for multi-turn red-teaming and safety evaluation.

b51e8d4d93490b72.title: Spectral Smoothing and Spiking Perturbations Reconfigure Capability Profiles and Selective Task Performance in Large Language Models
b51e8d4d93490b72.title_original: Spectral Smoothing and Spiking Perturbations Reconfigure Capability Profiles and Selective Task Performance in Large Language Models
b51e8d4d93490b72.summary: arXiv:2610.30676v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Singular-value spectra encode important structure in transformer feed-forward projections, yet their causal role in downstream behavior remains underexplored. We study post-hoc spectral smoothing and spiking interventions on the up_proj and down_proj matrices. Positive perturbation stretches deviations from the geometric mean, making large singular values larger and small ones smaller (spiking), and vice versa. The intervention preserves singular vectors and the geometric mean of the singular values. Across five open Llama and Qwen instruction models, we evaluate the perturbed systems on capability-labeled subtasks, standard and chain-of-thought reasoning benchmarks, judge-scored truthfulness, hallucination, and safety tasks, and TRAIT personality probes. To interpret score shifts, we fit responses in a three-dimensional capability basis consisting of factual knowledge, language understanding, and deductive reasoning. The induced changes suggest structured rather than purely random sensitivity: large positive perturbations more reliably suppress language and deductive responses, moderate negative perturbations can sometimes improve factual or task-local performance on the evaluated grids, and sensitivity varies strongly by model family, benchmark module, and underlying layerwise spectral inequality. These results position spectral perturbation as a lightweight intervention for probing how capabilities are organized and traded off in large language models.

bf05b4cba14fa874.title: Behavior Beyond Text: Evaluating Refusal Transfer Failure in LLM Agents
bf05b4cba14fa874.title_original: Behavior Beyond Text: Evaluating Refusal Transfer Failure in LLM Agents
bf05b4cba14fa874.summary: arXiv:2610.28982v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: While large language models are increasingly deployed as tool-calling agents, their safety evaluations still focus primarily on their ability to refuse harmful requests in text. We investigate whether the refusal behavior in text transfers to tool use. We construct a benchmark of 2,304 prompts across four domains, consisting of matched triplets that present the same harmful or benign request in text-only, standard tool-enabled, and adversarially framed tool-enabled settings. We then assess tool-call safety using 20 predefined forbidden actions. Testing five models of varying sizes and families, we find that requests refused in text frequently result in unsafe tool calls. Under standard tool-enabled prompting, this divergence occurs for 10-52 percent of harmful requests refused in chat. To mechanistically investigate this gap, we identify a refusal-associated direction in the residual stream of each of the five models. We find that in tool-enabled contexts, the activations along this direction decrease in four of five models. Furthermore, lower activation predicts unsafe tool calls across all five models (AUC 0.76-0.86). However, restoring the signal to the respective text-only value through activation patching only prevents a subset of unsafe calls, primarily by suppressing tool use rather than by producing safer calls. Steering along the refusal direction nearly eliminates unsafe calls only at strengths that also suppress benign tool use or degrade the output quality. Our findings indicate that the identified refusal direction contributes to whether a model acts, but only partially explains the refusal divergence. Therefore, evaluating the safety of tool-calling agents requires directly examining their actions along with their textual responses.

b2c2becf64c29ecf.title: GenXR-Bench: Benchmarking Coding Agents for Interactive XR Development
b2c2becf64c29ecf.title_original: GenXR-Bench: Benchmarking Coding Agents for Interactive XR Development
b2c2becf64c29ecf.summary: arXiv:2610.29014v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Coding agents are rapidly advancing from single-file generation to long-horizon repository-scale engineering, yet the evaluation of their capabilities to author interactive extended reality (XR) applications remains an open challenge. Unlike traditional software, XR applications operate within dynamic 3D physical environments where runtime robustness depends jointly on continuous user motion, spatial input, and environmental sensing. We introduce GenXR-Bench, the first benchmark for the end-to-end evaluation of coding agents in XR software development. GenXR-Bench contains 112 expert-authored tasks spanning 24 feature implementations, 21 bug repairs, and 67 application generation tasks. Held-out tests combine scripted and adaptive interactions with programmatic and visual assertions to evaluate core functionality and runtime behavior. GenXR-Bench's testing suite achieves 96.5% accuracy against blinded expert judgments of 124 candidate applications executed on consumer XR hardware. Evaluating 10 models on GenXR-Bench, we find that the strongest configuration achieves only 50.9% overall Pass@1. Failure analysis identifies recurring misunderstandings in asynchronous sensor lifecycles, physical grounding, and embodied interaction semantics. GenXR-Bench establishes a reproducible testbed for evaluating coding agents in the interactive and physically situated conditions of spatial computing.

bb43f2b59002ea5c.title: Industrial Agentic AI: LLM-Driven New-Generation Agents for Smart Manufacturing
bb43f2b59002ea5c.title_original: Industrial Agentic AI: LLM-Driven New-Generation Agents for Smart Manufacturing
bb43f2b59002ea5c.summary: arXiv:2610.26941v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are enabling agents to move beyond predefined workflows toward autonomous planning and execution, creating new opportunities for smart manufacturing. However, dynamic environments, complex physical constraints, and stringent reliability requirements hinder the direct deployment of general-purpose agents in smart manufacturing. This article presents a systematic overview of LLM-driven industrial agents. First, we analyze five key challenges and discuss the concept and core characteristics of industrial agents. We then establish a unified taxonomy covering application scenarios, embodiment forms, and five capability levels. Next, we propose a four-layer system architecture and detail its core modules and operational mechanisms for closed-loop task execution. Finally, we review representative applications across the industrial lifecycle and outline future research directions. This article provides a structured reference for the design, development, and application of industrial agents.

83d7eba918ac2cc2.title: MAMath-Bench: Process-Aware and Robust Evaluation of Multimodal Multi-Agent Mathematical Reasoning
83d7eba918ac2cc2.title_original: MAMath-Bench: Process-Aware and Robust Evaluation of Multimodal Multi-Agent Mathematical Reasoning
83d7eba918ac2cc2.summary: arXiv:2610.26943v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Mathematical reasoning is a fundamental capability for educational applications of Large Language Models (LLMs), where reliable problem solving requires not only correct answers but also coherent and verifiable reasoning processes. Multi-agent systems (MASs) have shown growing potential in this domain by leveraging collaboration and verification among multiple LLM agents. However, existing evaluations primarily focus on the correctness of final answers in text-only settings, offering limited insight into multimodal reasoning capabilities, the reliability of intermediate reasoning steps, and robustness against reasoning errors. To address these limitations, we introduce MAMath-Bench, a process-aware benchmark designed to evaluate the multimodal mathematical reasoning capabilities of MASs. MAMath-Bench comprises 1,003 problems spanning 11 mathematical categories, multiple difficulty levels, and several modalities, including text, images, and audio. It features fine-grained milestone annotations to evaluate systems across three dimensions: problem-solving correctness, reasoning-process reliability, and robustness to adversarial reasoning-chain perturbations. Our evaluation yields three key findings. First, multi-agent collaboration does not consistently improve final-answer accuracy over strong single LLMs. Second, collaboration can substantially enhance the coverage of intermediate reasoning, but such gains may come at the cost of increased reasoning redundancy. Third, current systems remain vulnerable to adversarial reasoning errors, particularly those involving subtle structural perturbations. The dataset is available at https://github.com/mira-ai-lab/AgentMath.

c5126e581aa15e99.title: Exploration via Activation-Space Steering for Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards
c5126e581aa15e99.title_original: Exploration via Activation-Space Steering for Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards
c5126e581aa15e99.summary: arXiv:2610.27012v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) trains a language model by sampling responses, scoring them with an automatic verifier, and updating the policy from the resulting rewards. The policy therefore receives direct learning signals only from trajectories that appear in its rollouts. Yet repeated sampling from the same policy can concentrate on similar reasoning paths, leaving useful alternatives unexplored under a fixed rollout budget. We introduce Activation-Space Exploration (ASE), an online method for diversifying training rollouts. By clustering activation differences between correct and incorrect responses to the same problem, ASE builds a structured bank of latent exploration vectors. Different vectors are then applied to subsequent rollouts to explore alternative reasoning paths. On Qwen3-1.7B-Base and Qwen3-8B-Base trained on DAPO-Math-17k, ASE improves average Mean@8 across six mathematical reasoning benchmarks over GRPO by 4.87 and 1.87 percentage points, respectively, under the same rollout budget.

7904968344458a95.title: Explore Separately, Adopt Selectively: Execution-Guided Tool Use over Large Tool Libraries
7904968344458a95.title_original: Explore Separately, Adopt Selectively: Execution-Guided Tool Use over Large Tool Libraries
7904968344458a95.summary: arXiv:2610.22688v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language model agents must discover relevant tools from large libraries, e.g., thousands of tools, as new needs arise during task execution. When several candidates could satisfy the same need, execution may be required to identify the relevant one. Investigating candidates in a shared trajectory can leave alternatives unexplored or allow failed attempts to influence subsequent reasoning. To address this, we present BRIA (BRanch-Inspect-Adopt), a simple yet effective agent that temporarily isolates candidate investigations in separate branches. Each branch retrieves and executes tools to investigate its candidate; a task agent inspects the resulting execution evidence and adopts only useful results into its continuing trajectory. BRIA retrieves additional tools as new capability needs arise during task execution. We evaluate BRIA on PlanBench-XL and MCP-Atlas using a shared pool of 1897 tools, three language models, and static and adaptive retrieval baselines. Across all settings, BRIA matches or exceeds the strongest retrieval baseline. On MCP-Atlas, it achieves an average claim score of 89.77, compared with 75.40 for MCP-Zero, a gain of 14.37 percentage points. BRIA also lies on the Pareto frontier for task performance and input-token cost.

c18d62280d4445b3.title_original: 英特尔面向四至六代至强处理器推出推理微服务：自动检测硬件并配置 vLLM 参数
c18d62280d4445b3.summary: IT之家 10 月 14 日消息，英特尔今日宣布推出 Intel Inference Microservices 服务，这是一套面向大语言模型推理的容器化微服务方案，目标是让企业在已有的至强处理器上直接获得经过调优的模型推理能力，无需再花费数天时间进行手动硬件优化。 在该模式下，每个微服务都是一个独立容器，通过 OpenAI 兼容 API 对外提供单个模型的服务，并在启动时自动检测所在的英特尔处理器型号，应用英特尔针对该模型和该硬件预先验证过的配置参数。 英特尔指出，让大语言模型给出回复并不困难，难的是在既有硬件上稳定、高质量地重复这一过程。精度设置、计算任务在核心之间的分配方式、内存跨 NUMA 节点的布局，以及推理引擎使用哪些指令集，都取决于模型本身和底层处理器。更换模型，合适的参数就变了；迁移到另一代芯片，参数又需要重新调整。英特尔推理微服务旨在将这一调优过程封装在容器内部 —— 用户选择模型，容器负责选择设置。首批版本基于 vLLM 引擎，支持 BF16 精度，可在 Docker 或 Kubernetes 1.24 及以上环境中运行，硬件要求为第四代、第五代或第六代英特尔至强处理器，建议配置 32GB 内存。 启动时，容器会检查主机的处理器代数、分配到的核心数量、NUMA 节点数量以及处理器内置的加速器。 英特尔特别强调了最后一项：近期至强核心内置了专门用于推理计算的引擎，包括用于矩阵乘法的英特尔高级矩阵扩展和用于周边计算的 AVX-512、AVX2 及 VNNI 向量扩展。这些加速器已经存在于用户现有的芯片中，但只有推理引擎知道它们存在并正确配置时才能发挥作用。 检测完成后，容器会选择经过验证的配置档案，解析调优后的引擎参数，缓存权重，并在指定端口启动推理服务。 对于运行特定模型镜像的用户，如果主机未被识别，容器会在启动时报错，而不是静默地以未调优状态运行。基础镜像则默认启用配置回退，在无匹配模型专用配置时，会采用与硬件兼容的通用配置。用户还可以通过命令行查看容器检测到的硬件信息和将要执行的 vLLM 命令，例如运行 detect-hardware 或 dry-run --format json 进行预检。 这并非英特尔首次涉足推理微服务领域。今年 9 月，英特尔开发者页面已介绍过 Intel AI for Enterprise Inference，一套面向至强处理器的开源 LLM 服务栈，同样基于 vLLM 架构。此次发布的推理微服务可以视为将这一能力进一步产品化、容器化，并纳入统一的推理接口蓝图之中。 英特尔在新闻稿中将当前版本定位为“迈向英特尔硬件统一推理的第一步”，明确表示这只是一个起点：至强处理器是开始的地方，而不是结束的地方。随着产品组合扩展到英特尔 GPU，包括代号 Crescent Island 的数据中心推理 GPU，同一微服务模式将延伸至 GPU 平台，变化的只是被选中的配置档案，应用程序所面对的接口保持不变。这意味着用户今天基于至强构建的推理工作负载，未来迁移到英特尔 GPU 时，只需更改部署配置，而无需重写应用程序或重新进行调优。 本次发布还包含一个值得注意的细节：微服务提供的接口刻意独立于底层芯片。一个模型对应一个容器，OpenAI 兼容 API 暴露在已知端口上，运行时自动检测平台并应用英特尔验证过的配置。这种稳定性并非打包层面的技巧，而是因为底层的优化工作被贡献到了开源上游项目中，而非锁定在厂商专属工具包内。 英特尔调优后的容器仍然是一个标准的 OpenAI 兼容端点，而不是必须采用的 SDK。英特尔计划在后续版本中增加 Helm Chart、Kubernetes Operator、更多推理引擎和精度支持。目前工具调用和结构化输出功能可作为 vLLM 的透传能力使用，但尚未被验证为正式支持的能力。每个模型附有各自的许可证，用户需自行确保部署行为符合许可条款。

9147d5b8d93dc3f2.title: IBM 与西门子合作推进纳米堆叠架构，加速 3D 晶体管量产进程
9147d5b8d93dc3f2.title_original: IBM 与西门子合作推进纳米堆叠架构，加速 3D 晶体管量产进程
9147d5b8d93dc3f2.summary: IT之家 10 月 14 日消息，今日，IBM 与西门子宣布达成一项新的研究合作，旨在推进 IBM 今年早些时候发布的纳米堆叠（nanostack）晶体管架构。 据 IBM 官方新闻稿，此次合作将结合 IBM 在半导体器件创新领域的领导地位与西门子在电子设计自动化（EDA）、工艺仿真、光刻优化及先进制造软件方面的专业能力，以加速纳米堆叠技术的开发。 据介绍，双方合作内容包括开发纳米堆叠的先进虚拟模型，以便在芯片制造之前对性能进行建模、优化设计并解决制造难题。 IBM 在今年 6 月首次发布了纳米堆叠架构，并称其为业界首个已知的三维纳米片设计。与当前将晶体管平铺在二维平面上并不断缩小间距的思路不同，纳米堆叠将晶体管垂直堆叠并错位排列，从而在相同面积内容纳更多晶体管。 在当前的 7 埃（0.7 纳米）节点下，该设计可在指甲盖大小的面积内集成近 1000 亿个晶体管，密度约为 IBM 2021 年发布的 2nm 测试芯片的两倍。该设计还允许在每个堆叠层中使用不同的材料组合，从而独立优化每个晶体管的性能和功耗。 IBM 此前公布的研究结果显示，与 2nm 节点相比，纳米堆叠架构在同等功耗下可提升高达 50% 的性能，或在同等性能下降低高达 70% 的功耗。 在 VLSI 2026 研讨会上，IBM 还报告了纳米堆叠在 SRAM（IT之家注：静态随机存取存储器）上实现 40% 的微缩改进，这对于 AI 工作负载所需的高带宽内存具有重要意义。 IBM 研究总监 Jay Gambetta 在发布会上表示：“我们不只是把晶体管做得更小，而是在重新发明芯片的构建方式，以提供显著更高的性能和能效。” IBM 硅技术研发副总裁 Huiming Bu 表示：“纳米堆叠是一个可扩展的晶体管平台，旨在将器件微缩从二维转向三维，代表了半导体行业的新范式，也是未来十年支持 AI 和其他新兴技术所需的逻辑微缩路径。” 西门子 EDA IC 组合执行副总裁 Ankur Gupta 则表示：“将半导体微缩推进到埃米时代，需要在器件物理、EDA 设计与制造软件以及制造之间进行紧密的协同优化。” IBM 曾表示，基于该技术的首批产品预计需要约五年时间才能由合作伙伴投入生产。此次与西门子的合作，正是为跨越这一从实验室到工厂的鸿沟而设。

64044568da6e2c6c.title: Hello Python 3.15, goodbye 3.10, and now I can use 3.11
64044568da6e2c6c.title_original: Hello Python 3.15, goodbye 3.10, and now I can use 3.11
64044568da6e2c6c.summary: Python 3.15 is here ! Here's the essential What's new in Python 3.15 guide, this year curated by 3.14 and 3.15 release manager Hugo van Kemenade. As someone who builds open source software that works in every supported Python version, I get to say goodbye to Python 3.10 and start embracing features from Python 3.11. First, some highlights from Python 3.15. Explicit lazy imports I'm most excited about Explicit lazy imports from PEP 810 . These let you import modules like so: lazy import json lazy from pathlib import Path The module will then be imported the first time those symbols are used in the code that follows. My LLM CLI tool implements plugins. I had to recommend manual lazy imports in the plugin author documentation, because simply installing plugins that used heavy dependencies such as sentence_transformers could add multiple seconds to every invocation of the llm command. Lazy imports directly address this startup cost. Unpacking in comprehensions The new [*sublist for sublist in lists] unpacking syntax is neat. Here's an illustration lifted from the documentation : lists = [[ 1 , 2 ], [ 3 , 4 ], [ 5 ]] [ * L for L in lists ] # [1, 2, 3, 4, 5] # equivalent to [x for L in lists for x in L] sets = [{ 1 , 2 }, { 2 , 3 }, { 3 , 4 }] { * s for s in sets } # {1, 2, 3, 4} # equivalent to {x for s in sets for x in s} dicts = [{ 'a' : 1 }, { 'b' : 2 }, { 'a' : 3 }] { ** d for d in dicts } # {'a': 3, 'b': 2} # equivalent to {k: v for d in dicts for k,v in d.items()} PEP 798: Unpacking in Comprehensions by Adam Hartz and Erik Demaine proposed this as an extension of the unpacking syntax from PEP 448 , which landed in Python 3.5 back in 2015. A sampling profiler Python's existing tracing profiler has been renamed from cProfile to profiling.tracing , and has been joined by an exciting new sampling profiler called Tachyon, aka profiling.sampling . Sampling profilers work by periodically capturing stack traces from running processes, then using those to calculate which functions have the most time spent inside of them. They're very low overhead and can provide a deep insight into running systems, without needing to instrument those systems first. I've previously used tools like py-spy for this. Now this capability is baked into the standard library. If you have the PID of an existing Python 3.15 process you can start gathering samples by running this (I had to use sudo on macOS): sudo uv run --python 3.15 python -m profiling.sampling attach 1234 Interact with the main program a bit, then hit Ctrl+C to stop gathering and see a report, which looks something like this: It can also produce flame graphs like this and heat maps like this , and can even output a format that can be viewed in the Firefox profiler UI. 3.15 isn't much faster than 3.14 Miguel Grinberg investigated How fast is Python 3.15? the other day against the 3.15.0rc3 release and found performance to be mostly the same as 3.14, with the exception of the experimental JIT. The JIT gave a 1.2x boost over the standard 3.15 interpreter (on a Fibonacci test), the first time Miguel observed a meaningful JIT performance increase. Miguel's explorations of 3.14 last year found significant boosts against Python 3.13 across many more categories. Upgrading to Python 3.15 with uv I used the following sequence of commands to get uv to use Python 3.15 on my Mac. First I had to upgrade uv itself to ensure it knew about the new release: uv self update Then I installed the stable 3.15 release: uv python install 3.15 And told uv that I wanted that to be the default for every uv run command, unless the project itself pinned a different version: uv python pin --global 3.15 Now the following reports 3.15 as the version: uv run python --version I already have a bunch of tools installed using uv tool install . I reinstalled them to use Python 3.15 like this: uv tool upgrade datasette --python 3.15 Then I can confirm the version like this: datasette --get /-/versions.json | jq Highlights from Python 3.11 The release of 3.15 means that Python 3.10 (released in 2021) is officially no longer supported . My policy for my main open source projects is to keep them working in every supported Python version. I can now drop 3.10 and start using features that were introduced in 3.11. Here's the What's new in Python 3.11 document. I finally get to rely on tomllib being available! Datasette makes extensive use of asyncio . 3.11 adds TaskGroup and timeout() , and several more new features. datetime.UTC is a new in 3.11 alias for datetime.timezone.utc . Python's SQLite support got some significant upgrades in 3.11, including: setlimit() and getlimit() expose a mechanism for setting SQLite runtime limits from Python. create_window_function() lets us create custom window functions in Python, as a class with step() , value() , inverse() , and finalize() methods. blobopen() provides an efficient mechanism for partial reads and writes of large BLOB binary values stored in a SQLite row. You can now call set_authorizer(None) to remove a SQLite authorizer. Datasette had a workaround for this! Plus a whole bunch of improvements to Python's typing system . I plan to land Python 3.11 improvements to a bunch of my projects over the next few weeks. Here's my first Datasette PR removing that set_authorizer(None) workaround. I've also updated my click-app , datasette-plugin , python-lib , and llm-plugin cookiecutter templates to test against Python 3.11 through Python 3.15. 86f334b4030daa87.title: eMudhra Intermediate CA Compromise
86f334b4030daa87.summary: eMudhra Intermediate CA Compromise This is very, very bad news: The private keys of eight eMudhra intermediate CA certificates have been compromised. They chain to roots trusted by the Mozilla, Microsoft, Apple and Chrome root programs and by many downstream trust stores. Any software that bundles a list of trusted certificates needs to be updated. This site is tracking software updates via this GitHub repository - Linux distros need to update their ca-certificates packages. In Python world uv 0.13.4 and pip 26.2.2 and certifi 2026.10.19 have been released with upgraded certificate lists. There's a very informative thread about this on the official Python forum. 936e8a2faa73fcf4.title: Introducing Kimi K3.1 Pro
936e8a2faa73fcf4.summary: Introducing Kimi K3.1 Pro Kimi K3.1 Pro landed on the Kimi API today - it's not yet open weights, but Moonshot promise "Full model weights will be released by Nov 4, 2026". They're also offering a "Highspeed" version that's 2-3x faster, at twice the price (except for input token cache hits, which are priced the same). The US dollar pricing is $2.00/million tokens for input and $10/million for output - the same as GPT-6.1 Sol and half the price of Claude Opus 5.5. Moonshot's own benchmarks show Kimi as approximately level with Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra - beating them on a few benchmarks, coming close on others. Artificial Analysis scored Kimi at 55 - ahead of Claude Fable 5.1, GPT-6 Astra, and Gemini 4 Argon (all at 53) and behind only Claude Opus 5.5 (58). This is the first time a (soon-to-be) open weight model has scored this highly against the frontier. I tried it out via the Moonshot API using the llm openai endpoint command I added to LLM 0.32 back in August: llm openai endpoint \ https://api.moonshot.ai/v1 \ --key kimi \ -m kimi-k3.1-pro \ "Generate an SVG of a pelican riding a bicycle" \ --responses \ -o reasoning_effort low \ > kimi-k3.1-pro-pelican-low.stdout.txt \ 2> kimi-k3.1-pro-pelican-low.stderr.txt llm openai endpoint can run prompts against any OpenAI-compatible endpoint but doesn't log the results, hence the extra options to save stdout and stderr (the reasoning trace). Here are the pelicans I got for Kimi K3.1 Pro on the three reasoning levels it supports - low, medium, and max. This is max: For comparison, I ran fresh pelicans against Kimi K3 on those three reasoning levels. 77b755c18da0e68a.title: Learning When to Withdraw: Curriculum Coverage and Rule-Specific Failures in Fine-Tuned Language Agents
77b755c18da0e68a.title_original: Learning When to Withdraw: Curriculum Coverage and Rule-Specific Failures in Fine-Tuned Language Agents
77b755c18da0e68a.summary: arXiv:2610.21045v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Tool-using language agents must revise prepared actions when evidence changes or authority is revoked. Selective withdrawal means suspending affected actions, preserving supported work, and resuming only after sufficient repair. We study supervised fine-tuning in NAQD-Env, a synthetic environment with explicit dependencies and a deterministic reference policy. Four LoRA checkpoints of Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct compare an original curriculum with an enriched one, the latter under three system-prompt framings with identical views and targets. Three instruction-tuned baselines and all four checkpoints are evaluated under three inference prompts on fresh validation cases, held-out dependency families, and held-out structural combinations. Under the naqd prompt, SFT checkpoints reach decision agreement of 0.77-0.92 and withdrawal recall of 0.46-0.86, versus 0.45-0.63 and at most 0.06 for the baselines. Rule-level diagnostics qualify these gains. The original-curriculum checkpoint wrongly withdraws 26 of 34 actions with surviving alternative support; enriched checkpoints withdraw 0-1. Conversely, all SFT checkpoints narrow prohibited combinations less often than the 7B and 8B baselines, a case absent from both curricula. Delegation results show more withdrawal but poorer preservation of independently authorized actions, and all four checkpoints omit valid event reports. Framing contrasts vary across metrics and splits and do not establish a reproducible advantage or equivalence. One training run per arm, jointly changed curriculum properties, prior evaluation exposure, and baseline-SFT quantization differences limit causal attribution. The contribution is a method for detecting rule-specific regressions that aggregate accuracy can conceal, not evidence that fine-tuning alone ensures agent safety.

8fc838e1f7b3f216.title: ClawLoop: Self-Improving Agents via Harness-Native Training Loop
8fc838e1f7b3f216.title_original: ClawLoop: Self-Improving Agents via Harness-Native Training Loop
8fc838e1f7b3f216.summary: arXiv:2610.14118v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The rapid advancement of Large Language Models (LLMs) has driven their deployment toward general-purpose harness environments, where LLM-based agents operate in sandbox workspaces and interact directly with file systems and shells. While numerous post-training pipelines exist for tool-use agents, their counterparts for harness-based agents remain scarce and are predominantly one-shot and teacher-dependent: a stronger external model synthesizes tasks and collects trajectories, the target agent is trained once, and evaluation results are consumed by human researchers rather than fed back into the loop. Such pipelines are inherently bounded by the capability of the external model and the scope of human prior, leaving no room for self-improvement. To address these limitations, we propose ClawLoop, a framework that enables self-improving without any external teacher model and with minimal prior dependencies. ClawLoop composes three phases into a self-sustaining cycle: Task Synthesis, which generates a diverse pool of training tasks via two complementary construction routines, applies diagnosis-conditioned difficulty growth followed by both agent-free and agent-based task validation; Training, which updates the agent via SFT and/or RL; and Diagnosis and Feedback, which analyzes the agent's rollout behaviors to produce a capability analysis report that will be used as feedback for task synthesis in the next iteration. Using Qwen3.6-27B as the loop model, ClawLoop yields consistent improvements on SkillsBench, Claw-Eval-Live, and ClawGym-Bench. The iteratively refined tasks are further transferred to smaller-scale Qwen3.5-4B and 9B models with gains across all benchmarks, validating data quality independently of the loop model.

93f750dd719898b1.title: Frustratingly Easy Agentic RAG via Portable Skills: A Case Study in Customer Support
93f750dd719898b1.title_original: Frustratingly Easy Agentic RAG via Portable Skills: A Case Study in Customer Support
93f750dd719898b1.summary: arXiv:2610.14428v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Enterprise workflow automation typically requires retrieving a complete and accurate set of relevant information from large operational document corpora (SOPs, policy documents) given a specific scenario or request. In customer support (CS), for example, human specialists must determine the correct sequence of resolution steps for each case, a task that demands precise grounding in policy documentation. Meeting this bar in production typically requires complex document chunking, indexing, and retrieval pipelines, often layered with learned re-rankers, query rewriters, and bespoke agentic RAG infrastructure. We report a deployment case study of a simpler alternative: a portable skill consisting of a natural-language instruction, lightweight tools (a retrieval API, format-checking scripts), and a corpus enriched with an LLM-generated navigation layer, which is a structured "Wikipedia-style" index over the underlying documents. This agentic RAG approach is straightforward to implement (1-2 engineer days), portable across capable agentic harnesses (e.g., Claude Code), and performs strongly on the challenging task of CS resolution workflow generation, achieving 99.2% procedural equivalence to human-approved ground truth and 83.3% evidence sufficiency. It is also roughly an order of magnitude slower per case than our deployed production assistant (~90 s vs. ~8-9 s), so we claim no latency advantage. Our claim is scoped to that setting: a mature, well-curated corpus, a latency-tolerant workflow, and human review of every case. There, the skill did the work of a complex RAG stack, and maintenance became a matter of editing text and data rather than retraining models.

1ecbf53f5f21672f.title: CLEAT: Learning Value-Guided Clarification for Interactive Agents
1ecbf53f5f21672f.title_original: CLEAT: Learning Value-Guided Clarification for Interactive Agents
1ecbf53f5f21672f.summary: arXiv:2610.12655v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: LLM agents can execute increasingly complex tasks, but effective assistance also requires aligning their actions with goals and constraints that users may leave unstated. We study this problem as interactive intent alignment through clarification. Yet clarification is useful only when the agent can turn the answer into better decisions. As training changes how the agent handles incomplete information and uses additional answers, the same clarification can become more or less useful. We introduce CLEAT (CLarification through valuE-guided Agent co-Training), a framework that co-trains a clarification-value controller and the task policy from shared interaction outcomes. We formulate residual query value to measure the task utility gained by asking rather than proceeding under the current policy, and estimate it through paired rollouts from the same interaction history. These paired returns train the controller to predict clarification value and the task policy to select useful questions and act on the answers. The controller guides subsequent rollout collection, while outcomes from the updated agent provide new value labels that allow clarification guidance to adapt as the agent learns. With Qwen3-4B, CLEAT achieves the highest mean score in all ten evaluation settings across four benchmarks. Gains over the strongest baseline reach 13.2 and 6.5 percentage points on UserGym Travel and IN3 underspecification judgment accuracy, respectively. Ablations show that co-training improves the task policy even when the controller is removed at inference, while adapting clarification guidance to the evolving policy yields further gains.

5744dd9420166428.title_original: EDWARD-NMT: Elastic Dimensions With Adaptive Routing and Dual-consistency for Neural Machine Translation
5744dd9420166428.summary: arXiv:2610.32115v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Sparse Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) is a powerful paradigm for scaling Neural Machine Translation (NMT) and managing language heterogeneity. However, practical limitations hinder its deployment on resource-constrained devices: the entire expert pool must remain in memory, and the per-token compute budget is statically fixed during training by rigid top-k routing. We introduce EDWARD-NMT (Elastic Dimensions With Adaptive Routing and Dual-consistency for NMT), a novel MoE encoder-decoder architecture designed for a train once, deploy anywhere paradigm that exposes a family of deployable sub-networks at inference time. EDWARD-NMT integrates three key innovations: (i) Matryoshka-style elastic dimensions to flexibly reduce the memory footprint; (ii) an adaptive sigmoid router with a learned, task-conditioned threshold, allowing each token to dynamically determine its active expert count; and (iii) a dual-consistency objective to maximize the performance of the extracted sub-networks. Extensive experiments on PhoMT (En-Vi), WMT-14 (En-De), multilingual OPUS-16, and a multi-domain De-En benchmark validate our approach. The full-capacity architecture matches or exceeds strong MoE baselines with improved parameter efficiency. Furthermore, the sub-networks seamlessly extracted from a single checkpoint consistently outperform comparably sized dense Transformers without any retraining.

f6b4809d5cdddcdb.title: PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agents via Machine-Checked Integrity Theorems and Scalable Community Trust
f6b4809d5cdddcdb.title_original: PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agents via Machine-Checked Integrity Theorems and Scalable Community Trust
f6b4809d5cdddcdb.summary: arXiv:2610.28987v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Persistent memory is a largely undefended surface for injection and poisoning, and the same risk limits memory sharing among agents. We present PerMIT, a memory architecture with provable integrity guarantees under an explicit trust assumption: only user-typed inputs and values confirmed at a gate are trusted. PerMIT mediates the release and use of untrusted environment-derived values through a finite memory interface, while preserving agent-driven multi-turn planning and tool choice. Over this finite interface, we prove two integrity theorems that are also machine-checked in Lean 4, which together ensure that environment-derived memory reaches a sensitive action only if confirmed at the gate and influences the agent's behavior only through what the gate displays. Every attack in our threat model thereby reduces to a single auditable decision, which a human, an LLM verifier, or both can make in practice. On Trojan Hippo, PerMIT records zero observed attack success with self-verification and lightweight verifiers. Because each confirmation is a logged verdict on exact content, endorsements accumulate across users, and sufficiently endorsed items become community-confirmed with no further verification required. Under explicit assumptions, we prove and corroborate in simulation a co-scaling property: as the community grows, the risks of promoting poison and of wrongly evicting benign knowledge fall, while per-user verification effort does not rise. On $\tau^2$-bench, communities of up to 90 autonomous agents use PerMIT to build shared knowledge bases with no direct memory injection promoted, and the resulting knowledge significantly improves new agents on held-out tasks, suggesting a path toward agents that safely self-improve at test time.

90b586b6cf5db7bb.title_original: D-Skill: Distilling Teacher Knowledge through Agent Skills
90b586b6cf5db7bb.summary: arXiv:2610.28914v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Frontier language-model agents excel at complex tasks, but high inference costs make transferring their capabilities to smaller models essential. Traditional knowledge distillation achieves this through parameter updates, requiring access to the student's weights and additional training compute while encoding the transferred knowledge implicitly in the parameters. We introduce D-Skill, a framework that treats the teacher as a black box and distills its behavioral advantage into an interpretable natural-language skill by analyzing paired rollouts and identifying behavioral divergences and agreements. The resulting lessons are consolidated offline, with any compatible skill-update backend, into a skill document that is provided to the student at inference time. D-Skill constructs the skill entirely offline from fixed trajectories, without labels, further environment interaction, or weight updates after rollout collection. Across SpreadsheetBench-Verified, ALFWorld, and chess puzzles spanning multiple teacher-student pairs, D-Skill closes 75%-95% of the teacher-student gap without touching model weights. After a single offline pass over the paired traces, D-Skill outperforms one-epoch SFT baselines and remains competitive with multi-epoch SFT. Under the same model family, the resulting student also incurs 5.7x-8.3x lower inference cost per task than the teacher. Our results demonstrate that natural-language skill distillation offers a performant, interpretable, and efficient alternative to weight-based capability transfer.

4ecfbdbc97d188f2.summary: arXiv:2610.30162v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Model fusion aims to integrate the capabilities of multi-expert models into a single model. Existing evaluations offer limited coverage of reasoning with long chains of thought and tool use, while strong average performance can mask substantial losses in individual expert capabilities. We introduce FusionEval, a benchmark that provides controlled expert pools, integrates fusion methods with and without additional training, and offers a unified evaluation suite. The pools contain domain experts independently trained from Qwen3 and Llama base models across math, code, science, instruction following, and tool use. Extensive experiments show that training-free methods preserve reasoning performance but substantially degrade tool use at both model scales. In contrast, MOPD preserves tool use and achieves a more balanced capability profile, but requires additional data preparation, inference, and training. Jointly retaining reasoning, instruction following, and tool use at low computational cost remains a challenge. We hope FusionEval supports future research on efficient model fusion that jointly preserves expert capabilities. Our code is available at https://github.com/Baicaihaochi/FusionEval_Benchmark.

Still, these methods introduce the additional question of how to assign credit to each attempt. We propose to view the credit assignment through the lens of Stochastic Shortest Paths, a framework in classical reinforcement learning that seeks to minimize the expected cumulative cost to reach a terminal state (in our case, a verified successful response). On Qwen3-0.6B, ReAPO also outperforms GRPO with twice the group size or twice the training steps, reaching their peak accuracy with 39% and 31% fewer generated tokens, respectively. 899f86d735098d72.title_original: Does Multi-Agent Collaboration Reduce Hallucination in Clinical Tasks?
899f86d735098d72.summary: arXiv:2610.27027v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multi-agent LLM systems improve performance on clinical tasks, and that improvement is often read as evidence of a more trustworthy system. However, the two are not the same claim. A clinician acts on the stated reasoning and not only on the conclusion, so whether collaboration reduces hallucination, and what decides when it does, has to be measured in the reasoning too. Yet most evaluations score only the final answer. We evaluate four systems (a single-LLM baseline and three multi-agent topologies) across four models and three clinical tasks, scoring hallucination, under a factuality and faithfulness taxonomy, inside the rationale each system generates and reporting it alongside the task metric. We report that collaboration buys task performance but not lower hallucination as a rule, and no topology is reliably better than another. The effect differs by model: of the $36$ model--system--task comparisons, $12$ are large enough to resolve --- four decreases and eight increases, with no model on both sides. What sets the level, and the direction of any change, is the model rather than the topology or the number of agents. A self-correction experiment is consistent with this: shown its own flagged errors, every model except Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct reduces hallucination; the one model for which collaboration lowers hallucination gains the most, and Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct, the model whose hallucination it amplifies most, does not reduce its hallucination at all. We find that collaboration redistributes what its models can already do; it does not supply what they cannot.

8beb0466d6dd3e57.title: SANE: Automated Scorer-Specific Metamorphic Testing for LLM Judges
8beb0466d6dd3e57.title_original: SANE: Automated Scorer-Specific Metamorphic Testing for LLM Judges
8beb0466d6dd3e57.summary: arXiv:2610.28886v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: LLM judges increasingly mediate benchmark evaluation, model selection, data curation, and training. Their decisions are useful only when each judge responds reliably to changes affecting its scoring criterion. Existing methods for reliability testing perturb inputs with known expected effects on judge scores. Prominent LLM-judge testing harnesses combine human-authored perturbation recipes with synthetic test generation, leaving scorer-specific recipe ideation outside the automated pipeline. This limits their use to fixed perturbations and pre-assumed scorer types. We introduce SANE, an agent-based framework that encodes behavioral requirements for stochastic evaluators as reusable agent instructions. Given a scorer specification, implementation, and representative inputs, the pipeline first identifies scorer-specific capabilities, then automatically derives perturbation recipes and expected score relations for each. SANE also defines a scorer-independent validation framework for generated judge tests. It determines whether each recipe agrees with scorer intent and whether each instantiated case realizes the recipe and supports its expected relation. Because SANE generates a recipe inventory tailored to each scorer, the number of aligned recipes grows as scorers are added. Across five domains, SANE produces 3.7 times as many validated test families as the Judge Reliability Harness (JRH) at comparable end-to-end validity and detects scorer deficiencies in every domain, including professionalism and toxicity, where JRH detects none. On faithfulness, SANE achieves strong human alignment in judge ranking: its test-suite scores rank 11 judge models consistently with human-labeled FaithBench performance (Spearman rho = 0.852), while JRH does not (rho = 0.100).

6b082082a77492f6.title: High-dimensional layer-state trajectories reveal the internal dynamics of transformer inference
6b082082a77492f6.title_original: High-dimensional layer-state trajectories reveal the internal dynamics of transformer inference
6b082082a77492f6.summary: arXiv:2610.26866v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Mechanistic studies of large language models localize function in parameters, attention heads or neurons, but those parts do not specify how one inference unfolds. We treat the ordered layer-state trajectory as the empirical process and test whether layer order defines a measurable computation. Across representative Qwen, Llama and Gemma checkpoints, realized order produced paths 1.60--2.24 times as aligned with their endpoint chord as endpoint-preserving shuffles. The order effect transferred to a lexical task, but was stronger in three random initializations of the same Qwen architecture, identifying an architecture-compatible scaffold rather than a training-specific law. Direct hidden states provided stronger mechanism coordinates than vocabulary readbacks, and a task-defined coordinate made candidate competition computable. After additive interventions failed, local transition actuators selectively controlled internal trajectories across checkpoints. A confidence gate then drove 17 of 87 held-out Qwen closure trajectories across the full-vocabulary top-1 candidate boundary while leaving all 203 non-closure top-1 outputs unchanged. Safety-matched action reassignment performed similarly, locating the gain in selective gating and the bounded actuator family rather than fine-grained dose assignment. Layer order exposes an observable, computable and behaviourally consequential process of transformer inference without establishing a complete theory of LLM dynamics or control of answer correctness.

0469c4212af59849.title: LoWAgent: A Low-Resource Multilingual Benchmark for Web Agents
0469c4212af59849.title_original: LoWAgent: A Low-Resource Multilingual Benchmark for Web Agents
0469c4212af59849.summary: arXiv:2610.27205v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Web agents are typically evaluated on English-language interfaces, leaving their ability to operate across the world's multilingual websites largely unexplored. This gap is especially significant for low-resource languages, where standardized resources for evaluating web agents remain limited. To address this gap, we introduce Low-Resource Web Agent Benchmark (LoWAgent), a benchmark for evaluating web agents across different low-resource languages (LRLs) in comparison to the default, English. LoWAgent evaluates web agents across English and four LRLs: Hindi, Bengali, Urdu, and Amharic. The benchmark comprises of six fully localized websites, instantiated across five languages to yield 3,000 task instances. We evaluate three closed-source and five open-source models across all five languages on all six websites. Our findings show that both closed-source and open-source models experience performance degradation for LRLs compared to English, with substantially greater performance drops observed among the open-source model agents. We further evaluate the robustness of the models on realistic interface disruptions, such as cookie notices and advertisement pop-ups, and find that these further degrade agentic performance. Finally, we show that post-training on a small subset of LoWAgent traces can significantly improve low-resource language agentic task performance, demonstrating the usefulness of our benchmark.

03f16ec76810e3c4.title: Do We Need the Largest LLMs for Every Clinical Decision?
03f16ec76810e3c4.title_original: Do We Need the Largest LLMs for Every Clinical Decision?
03f16ec76810e3c4.summary: arXiv:2610.26937v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large clinical language models often require multi-GPU infrastructure, limiting local deployment. We introduce CERTA, a decision-level statistical certificate that determines when a quantized model may substitute for its native BF16 reference and escalates decisions that cannot be certified to it. Across eleven instruction-tuned models, both general-purpose and domain-adapted, from three families (7-72B), we evaluated 2,500 clinical-verification decisions from de-identified patient contexts (2,484 patients), with patient-disjoint calibration and testing. In the higher-power operational analysis, round-to-nearest 8-bit quantization at BF16 storage served 99.8-100% of held-out decisions across all eleven models; formal finite-sample guarantees were assessed separately using the exact split-sample procedure. In the same operational analysis, the class-conditional 4-bit frontier reduced the amortized, BF16-equivalent deployment cost to 25.8% and 27.3% of the BF16 reference for Qwen2.5-72B and HuatuoGPT-o1-72B, respectively, with measured peak memory of 43.0 and 42.7 GB, below the nominal capacity of a single 48 GB accelerator. Deployment on that specific hardware was not directly tested. Under the exact split-sample certificate, which also accounts for configuration selection, these costs were 26.7% and 27.9%. On external disease named-entity benchmarks against human annotations, the frontier-selected NF4 configurations had a mean absolute F1 change of 0.045 on both datasets, with substantial model-specific variation. CERTA converts compression from a fixed precision choice into a risk-controlled deployment policy for this verification task.

fffb20965f063b07.title: Testing the Planning Claims of LLM-Based Agents against Formal Semantics
fffb20965f063b07.title_original: Testing the Planning Claims of LLM-Based Agents against Formal Semantics
fffb20965f063b07.summary: arXiv:2610.22469v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: LLM-based agents are increasingly credited with the competences of practical reasoning: planning, monitoring, and correcting their own actions. Their success is attributed to the prompting strategies and agent architectures built around the model, such as chain-of-thought, search-based prompting, self-refinement, reflection, critics and tool-using loops. Yet these claims are usually supported by end-to-end success rates, which show only whether a task was completed, or by LLM judges, which are not verifiers. We test LLM planning against formal semantics. Tasks are posed in natural language, but each is grounded in a hidden PDDL model that decides whether every action is applicable, whether the goal is reached, and whether a plan exists at all. Across five domains (two of them new, all released with the paper), four models, six prompting strategies and three agent architectures, the best configuration solves 78% of the solvable tasks offline but only 40% online, where agents mostly act without inspecting the state. Unsolvable tasks are recognised in under 10% of episodes, and heavier prompting strategies use 5 to 22 times as many tokens as direct prompting with no clear gain. In our experiments, planning performance varied more across models than across prompting strategies or agent architectures. Claims that agents can plan require evidence from validated action traces.

c9abaa7f856798b7.title: Compression Precedes, Content Decides: Emergent Misalignment in Reward Models
c9abaa7f856798b7.title_original: Compression Precedes, Content Decides: Emergent Misalignment in Reward Models
c9abaa7f856798b7.summary: arXiv:2610.22805v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Emergent Misalignment - the out of domain generalization of narrow harmful fine-tuning first shown by Betley et al. [2025] has been widely studied in language models but not in reward models that supervise them. In this paper, we fine-tune two state-of-the-art reward models, Skywork-Reward-V2-Llama-3.1-8B and Skywork-Reward-V2-Qwen3-8B [Liu et al., 2025] and show that narrow fine-tuning reward models to prefer harm in one domain (medical or financial) generalizes to seven held out domains. This is not degeneracy, as the fine-tuned reward models lose only 4.8 and 5.3 points overall (RM-Llama) on the standard RewardBench 2 evaluation [Malik et al., 2025] while still outperforming the unmodified RM-Qwen model. We then fine-tune the underlying language models, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct and Qwen3-8B using DPO [Rafailov et al., 2023] and SFT on the same data. We find that reward models are more vulnerable to preference inversions compared to their language model counterparts. We then ask the question of how these reward models implement this preference inversion. Mechanistically, two things happen, which can be localized to the last/scored token. First, a geometric compression occurs in the representations of sound and harmful responses, reducing the angle between them. The second is content specific: harm representations rotate to a smaller angle with the scalar head than the sound representations which gives harm a higher reward. This happens only in harmful preference fine-tunes and not in control.

b5bdb36475b9e637.title: Author-in-the-loop Agentic Reproducibility Auditing for a Machine Learning Conference
b5bdb36475b9e637.title_original: Author-in-the-loop Agentic Reproducibility Auditing for a Machine Learning Conference
b5bdb36475b9e637.summary: arXiv:2610.22465v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Reproducibility checks during peer review require a shared understanding of what authors' code is expected to reproduce. We present an author-in-the-loop collaborative audit that makes author declarations explicit inputs to an AI agent's investigation and assessment. A structured checklist records reproduction instructions and limitations; a two-stage workflow on GitHub connects agent checks to author clarification, revision, and agent reassessment. The agent separately assesses whether results have been reproduced and whether authors need to provide clarification or make repairs, while human reviewers approve requests and decide whether concerns are resolved. We deployed the system across 36 conference papers and 133 experimental tables and figures, raising 20 issues after human review. Further checks supported closing all the issues, although full reproduction remained unverified in some cases. We further compared repeated audits with complete and blank checklists to examine how author declarations shaped the agent's investigation and assessment. Our work contributes a collaborative workflow and agent design that use author knowledge to guide reproducibility auditing. The conference deployment provides empirical evidence that this approach can help identify and address reproducibility problems through collaboration among authors, agents, and reviewers.

7e9f1dc1086f8a2f.title: ECHOES: Seeing Beyond the Current Image via Recursive History Compression and Privileged On-Policy Distillation
7e9f1dc1086f8a2f.title_original: ECHOES: Seeing Beyond the Current Image via Recursive History Compression and Privileged On-Policy Distillation
7e9f1dc1086f8a2f.summary: arXiv:2610.22408v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Long-horizon GUI agents rely on visual history to maintain task states, but retaining historical screenshots increases visual-token usage and inference costs, while textual summaries can discard critical state information, undermining long-horizon reliability. We propose ECHOES, which leverages training-time privileged information to guide textual history compression and strengthen long-horizon reasoning. Specifically, ECHOES adopts a Compression-Think-Action (CTA) format to recursively update a textual history state and reason. The same model, given privileged multi-image inputs, serves as a teacher that provides dense token-level on-policy distillation on student-generated CTA rollouts. Our Perception-Memory Fidelity (PMF) Gap-guided OPD-RL framework dynamically balances privileged distillation and task-reward optimization, with periodic teacher updates supporting continued improvement. We further introduce ECHOESBMK, a fine-grained diagnostic benchmark derived from real GUI agent failure trajectories to jointly evaluate visual perception and cross-modal state retention. Experiments on four GUI benchmarks and ECHOESBMK demonstrate substantial gains in task performance and memory fidelity. Without retaining historical screenshots at deployment, ECHOES achieves competitive performance with a favorable performance-inference-cost trade-off and exhibits positive zero-shot transfer to unseen visual planning tasks.

334791e5f2f5bb76.summary: IT之家 10 月 26 日消息，据 TechCrunch 报道，私募巨头阿波罗全球管理公司（Apollo Global Management）首席经济学家近期发布研报提出一个观点：科技行业之外，还没有任何大型企业从 AI 身上赚到实打实的利润增量。 IT之家注意到，阿波罗的托斯滕 · 斯洛克（Torsten Slok）重点观察了他所称的标普 493 指数成分股，也就是标普 500 剔除 Alphabet、亚马逊、苹果、Meta、微软、英伟达、特斯拉这七家科技巨头之后剩下的公司。数据显示，这批企业的利润率、人均营收基本持平，没有证据证明 AI 提升了它们的生产效率。 斯洛克写道：“尽管 AI 投入巨大、宣传铺天盖地，但对美国企业而言，科技行业以外，这项技术还没有带来任何财务回报。” 这会不会只是非科技企业落地节奏落后于科技巨头？斯洛克对此持怀疑态度。他认为，美国普通企业很难把越来越廉价的智能算力转化成更高营收增速和利润率。 “AI 或许是一个强大的计算器，但商业里需要的智能，大多是判断力。”他还补充道：“AI 理解不了责任、信任、企业文化、潜规则、伦理取舍与公平性，而这些因素决定声誉风险，最终左右营收增长与利润率。” 近期也有多项研究得出相近结论：AI 至今还没能带来显著的生产率提升。

c707f471c3a3d346.title: 软银投资的农业无人机创企极飞科技：希望让每个农民都有自己的机器人
c707f471c3a3d346.title_original: 软银投资的农业无人机创企极飞科技：希望让每个农民都有自己的机器人
c707f471c3a3d346.summary: IT之家 10 月 25 日消息，据英国《金融时报》今天（25 日）上午报道，获得软银投资的中国农业无人机企业极飞科技，希望让“每个农民都有自己的机器人”。面对农业劳动力持续减少、气温不断升高，极飞认为， 无需飞手操控的植保无人机 能够帮助农民应对双重挑战。 按营收计算，极飞是 仅次于大疆的全球第二大农业无人机制造商 。公司推出了一系列配套自动化无人机场的产品，无人机降落后可自动完成清洗、充电和补充药液，系统还能自行规划喷洒航线。 极飞科技高级副总裁龚槚钦指出， 缺少劳动力、农业从业人员老龄化 ，是中国农场面临的两大难题，许多农场还难以找到有空前来喷洒作业的无人机飞手。气候变化使天气更加极端，也让农业智能化、自动化变得愈发迫切。“未来每个农民都会有自己的机器人。这将带来革命性的改变，因为我们认为，眼下制约无人机行业发展的最大障碍就是飞手。” 龚槚钦指出，飞手往往希望尽快喷完一处农田，再赶往下一处，偏远地区的农场也很难吸引飞手上门。 推动农业走向自动化的另一股力量，是农业劳动力的快速流失。“AI 公司谈估值和市场规模，看的是能替代多少人。我们恰好相反：未来五年会失去多少劳动力，就意味着多大的市场规模。” 龚槚钦估算，中国每年约有 1200 万人从农村迁往城市。按照人口流动的速度， 未来三年中国需要 300 万架无人机 ；如果要覆盖全国所有耕地，无人机需求量最高可达 1200 万架。 极飞的无人机、农业无人车和农田传感器销往近 70 个国家，包括美国、巴西以及非洲和东南亚多地。 极飞成立于 2007 年，最初经营面向普通消费者的航模品牌，目前正筹备赴港上市。根据 Caplight 的估算，极飞在 2023 年一轮融资中的估值约为 15 亿美元 （IT之家注：现汇率约合 100.34 亿元人民币） ，软银持股 12.9%。 龚槚钦预计，为应对劳动力紧缺，未来十年中国以外的农场 可能需要 500 万至 1000 万架无人机 。 美国严格限制新款中国无人机的销售，已从极飞最大的海外市场退居第二位，巴西则升至首位。龚槚钦认为，今后开拓美国市场“会更加困难”。尽管如此，极飞最近 仍获得了监管部门的批准 ，可以在美国销售最新型号的无人机。 他还指出，面对气候变化的威胁，即使是最习惯传统耕作方式的农民，也开始改变对无人机等新技术的态度。“技术、天气和劳动力短缺交织在一起…… 农民面对的情况变得非常复杂，承受的压力也很大。”

6eb9e7b14f819904.title: 戴尔推出 UltraSharp“焕新版”4K 显示器：32 英寸 5199 元，27 英寸 3999 元
6eb9e7b14f819904.title_original: 戴尔推出 UltraSharp“焕新版”4K 显示器：32 英寸 5199 元，27 英寸 3999 元
6eb9e7b14f819904.summary: IT之家 10 月 24 日消息，戴尔京东自营店新上了两款 UltraSharp“焕新版”显示器，但本质上是一次渠道型号的调整。 其中，32 英寸的 U3226QER 定价 5199 元，IT之家此前已有报道；27 英寸的 U2726QER 到手价 3999 元。Chiphell 论坛上有用户挖掘发现，两款型号分别对应此前的 U3225QE 和 U2725QE，新旧型号被列为衍生关系，共用相同的面板与光学测试数据，功耗指标也完全一致。两者最直观的区别在边框颜色：U3226QER 和 U2726QER 改为银色支架与银色背板，前代则为黑色。 两款显示器均采用进阶版 IPS Black 面板，对比度 3000:1，峰值亮度 600 尼特，支持 10-Bit 色彩和 120Hz 刷新率。 差异主要出现在 HDR 认证上：32 英寸 U3226QER 支持 HDR 600，27 英寸 U2726QER 为 HDR 400。 色彩覆盖方面，两者均标称 100% sRGB、100% BT.709、99% DCI-P3 和 99% Display P3，出厂校色全屏色准 ΔE＜1.5，并搭载戴尔控色系统用于色彩校准。护眼部分通过 TUV 五星锐视认证，硬件级防蓝光相比上一代减少 15% 有害蓝光。 接口配置是这一代 UltraSharp 的延续性优势，两款机型均提供 3 个 HDMI 2.1、1 个雷电 4 上行接口（140W 供电，支持 DP 1.4）、1 个雷电 4 下行接口（15W，支持菊花链）、1 个 10Gbps USB-C、4 个 10Gbps USB-A、2.5GbE RJ45 网口以及音频输出，并配有弹出式 USB Hub，内含 1 个 USB-A 和 2 个 USB-C。支架支持 150mm 高度调节、-5° 至 21° 俯仰、±45° 左右旋转和 ±90° 垂直旋转，底座尺寸经过收窄，对小桌面更友好。 京东 戴尔（DELL）UltraSharp 27 英寸 4K 显示器 IPS Black 120Hz 防蓝光  140W 雷电 4 适配 macOS U2725QE 焕新版 U2726QER 券后 3999 元 领 300 元券 相关阅读： 《 戴尔推出“U3226QER”31.5 英寸显示器：4K 120Hz IPS Black 面板、双雷电 4 接口，5199 元 》 《 消息称戴尔显示器已发布内部通知，本月正式开始上调出货价 》 京东 11.11 无门槛红包 面额至高 26888 元，每天抽 3 次： 点此抽红包 。 淘宝 11.11 无门槛红包 面额至高 26888 元，每天抽 1 次： 点此抽红包 。

125b2f62831034f3.summary: IT之家 10 月 21 日消息，在 2026 世界智能网联汽车大会上，蔚来创始人、董事长、CEO 李斌分享了一组最新数据： 截至目前，基于世界模型架构 + 闭环强化学习的蔚来智能辅助驾驶系统， 已经部署在超过 95 万辆智能电动汽车上 ； 智能辅助驾驶安全行驶里程超过 91.4 亿公里， 累计使用时长达到 1.12 亿小时 ，为用户避免或减轻了 907 万次潜在事故影响； 根据内部数据， 人车共驾的平均安全里程达到人驾的 8 倍 。根据四家保险公司的数据佐证，搭载蔚来智能辅助驾驶系统的车辆，事故安全损失逐年降低，降幅超 30%。 据IT之家今日早些时候报道，李斌在 2026 世界智能网联汽车大会的对话环节中提出，自动驾驶进入“下半场”后，衡量其价值的标准需要回到两个可以被验证的指标上。 李斌将这两个指标概括为：用户是否愿意为自动驾驶功能付钱，以及自动驾驶能否让用户显著感知到它比人开车更安全。他直言， 如果用户不愿意付钱，自动驾驶讲得再好，也没有真正创造用户价值 。

7ad74055b3fea187.title: 腾讯云宣布元宝搜索对外开放：已构建千亿级索引规模，定价每千次 14 元起
7ad74055b3fea187.title_original: 腾讯云宣布元宝搜索对外开放：已构建千亿级索引规模，定价每千次 14 元起
7ad74055b3fea187.summary: IT之家 10 月 21 日消息，腾讯云 10 月 20 日宣布， 元宝搜索 正式通过腾讯云对外开放。 腾讯云介绍称，过去一年，元宝持续打磨搜索体验与效率，整合全网公开资源和腾讯优质内容，将大模型技术应用于内容收录、理解与检索全链路，构建面向大模型和 Agent 的搜索引擎。 目前， 元宝搜索构建了千亿级的索引规模，日均调用量达数亿次 ，全面支撑了 WorkBuddy、ima、腾讯金融科技、腾讯视频等 50 多个核心业务的搜索服务。 WorkBuddy：检索技术文档、官方 API 等一手资料，减少工具调用和模型轮次 ima：结合知识库与公网信息，有效信源召回量提升约 10% 腾讯视频：支持根据剧情、模糊描述找片，信息覆盖度扩展 20% 腾讯金融科技：一周上线金融搜索能力，大幅降低开发和运维成本 元宝搜索结合全网公开资源与腾讯内容生态，接入金融、医疗、法律、出行等 13 个垂直行业的 157 个信源 ，包括申万宏源、携程、飞常准、腾讯医典、腾讯地图等。A 股、港股、美股、日股、韩股财报收录覆盖率达 99% 以上。 内容入库前，大模型会解析网页并保留标题、表格等结构，从站点、账号、页面三个层面评估质量， 优先选择权威来源，过滤低质内容 。 元宝搜索还支持政策、新闻、天气、行情等内容实现 分钟级更新 ，并根据查询时间组织结果。例如查询世界杯赛程，优先返回即将进行的比赛和最近比分，避免近期赛事因长度限制被截断。 专业查询还需要业务知识。例如“明天北京飞上海的航班”，接口需要的是机场代码。元宝搜索通过垂直领域知识库与映射规则， 将城市、机场名称转换为接口可识别的参数，处理名称差异与歧义 。 获取候选资料后，元宝搜索综合相关性、时效性与权威性进行排序。对于需要多份资料才能回答的问题，元宝搜索会从整体上筛选相互补充的内容，用尽量少的文档覆盖核心信息，减少重复、冲突和遗漏。 Agent 的一次提问通常会拆成 3 到 5 个子问题，还可能调用 10 多个外部服务，任何环节变慢都会拉长整体等待。元宝搜索围绕响应速度做了多项系统优化。 元宝搜索提供三种版本服务 检索层，元宝搜索首创倒排索引、向量索引、融合提效三类索引融合架构，在同一套系统中兼顾关键词精确匹配与语义检索，通过共享特征与存储减少冗余开销， 保持 94% 高召回率的同时，实现底层索引检索平均耗时 8 毫秒 。 排序层，文档内容预先压缩为约 100 个标记并缓存，排序时直接复用，无需重复处理全文， 核心排序模型的推理耗时由 149 毫秒降至 30 毫秒 。 链路层，元宝搜索为每个环节单独设定耗时上限，外部服务响应超时即自动降级，避免单一环节的延迟影响整体响应。在元宝 App 中， 端到端响应时间缩短近 1 秒 。 IT之家查询发现，元宝搜索可选极速版、标准版、旗舰版，定价为每千次 14 元起。用户可通过检索词发起请求，接口以 JSON 形式返回搜索结果对应的排序信息、数据字段。

56d947377d09ce1e.title: RoLaQ: Joint Rotation and Range Calibration for 2-Bit KV Caches in Multi-Head Latent Attention
56d947377d09ce1e.title_original: RoLaQ: Joint Rotation and Range Calibration for 2-Bit KV Caches in Multi-Head Latent Attention
56d947377d09ce1e.summary: arXiv:2610.20686v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multi-head latent attention (MLA) compresses the content of a key-value cache into a shared latent per token, making low-bit storage attractive for long-context inference. At two bits, errors in this representation perturb both attention matching and value readout, with effects that depend on error direction and reconstruction scale. We introduce RoLaQ (Rotation-calibrated Latent Quantization), an offline method for joint rotation and range calibration. RoLaQ refines a shared rotation within subspaces defined by the frozen key and value projections, and jointly learns quantization ranges whose thresholds and reconstruction gains are coupled to control the shared signal's response. Prediction matching and attention-output supervision guide calibration with model weights frozen. Across three MLA models and six benchmarks, RoLaQ achieves the highest average accuracy among the compared 2-bit methods both without and with token protection. On DeepSeek-V2-Lite, an SGLang implementation provides 3.96 times the BF16 KV capacity under the same memory budget and 2.51 times its decode throughput with 256K input tokens.

a2a3c1dedfb77584.title: Inverse Reasoning Models for Efficient Post-Training and Verification from Answer-Only Data
a2a3c1dedfb77584.title_original: Inverse Reasoning Models for Efficient Post-Training and Verification from Answer-Only Data
a2a3c1dedfb77584.summary: arXiv:2610.18878v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Post-training reasoning LLMs often requires making a tradeoff between costly supervision and compute inefficiency: supervised finetuning typically requires reasoning traces, which is data inefficient since in many applications one only has prompt-answer tuples and lacks the groundtruth chain-of-thought (CoT) sequence. On the other hand, reinforcement learning (with verifiable rewards, for example) can operate without CoT data but it is much more compute-inefficient since it requires multiple autoregressive completions per optimization step, none of which are guaranteed to give a non-zero policy gradient. In this work we explore a middleground, a self-distillation technique that uses answer-only data, treating CoT as latent variables. This relies on training a partner ``inverse reasoning LLM" that generates the original's reasoning traces conditioned on the answer. The inverse model is trained once and reused across incoming batches of answer-only data, with all generation happening offline and up front, making the approach particularly suited to continual post-training. Using Qwen3-0.6B on the Countdown and GSM8K tasks, we show that after GRPO training has saturated, a single offline distillation round from the inverse model roughly doubles pass@1 on hard prompts and, on Countdown, outperforms rejection-sampling self-distillation on every hard-tail metric at every mix ratio (with smaller gains on GSM8K); rejection sampling by construction has no signal on problems the model never solves on its own. Continued GRPO on the fresh data retains an edge at hard pass@1 but trails distillation at pass@8 and pass@32 while regenerating rollouts at every step. As an added bonus we see that the inverse model has a second application as an accurate verifier of correctness. When used for best-of-$n$ selection at test time, it raises selection accuracy on Countdown from 0.753 (majority voting) to 0.969.

f35ddbfa2d1fb5f1.title: Unlocking Structured Pruning for Reasoning Language Models via Attention-Preserving MLP Trimming
f35ddbfa2d1fb5f1.title_original: Unlocking Structured Pruning for Reasoning Language Models via Attention-Preserving MLP Trimming
f35ddbfa2d1fb5f1.summary: arXiv:2610.19121v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Structured pruning reduces LLM inference costs by removing model components to produce smaller dense models. However, existing methods can cause reasoning performance to collapse on long-form reasoning tasks such as AIME. We propose \textit{LayerTrim}, a training-free structured pruning method that identifies redundant decoder layers and selectively trims their MLP features while preserving attention and decoder depth. LayerTrim is the first training-free structured pruning method designed to preserve long-form reasoning without gradients or recovery training. Across three reasoning language models and five benchmarks, LayerTrim outperforms existing structured pruning methods in most evaluated settings, improving average accuracy by up to 21.4 percentage points over RESP. On \texttt{Qwen3-14B}, LayerTrim achieves 1.24$\times$ faster prefill and 19.7\% lower peak GPU memory than the dense model, while better preserving reasoning ability. It also achieves the shortest average generation length among evaluated pruned models, while retaining the highest average accuracy. These results demonstrate that LayerTrim improves reasoning efficiency through both structural compression and reduced token generation.

1cee6de6907ebf4a.title: 英伟达发布 DGX Station for Windows：本地运行 1 万亿参数 AI 模型，最高 748GB 内存
1cee6de6907ebf4a.title_original: 英伟达发布 DGX Station for Windows：本地运行 1 万亿参数 AI 模型，最高 748GB 内存
1cee6de6907ebf4a.summary: IT之家 10 月 8 日消息，太平洋时间 10 月 7 日上午 10 点（北京时间 10 月 8 日凌晨 1 点）在美国旧金山举办的发布会上，英伟达发布 DGX Station for Windows， 定位为桌面级 AI 超级计算机，旨在让开发者、研究人员和数据科学团队在本地运行大规模 AI 模型，将于 2026 年第四季度上市。 IT之家援引博文介绍，DGX Station 搭载 NVIDIA GB300 Grace Blackwell Ultra Desktop Superchip，配备 72 核 Grace CPU、Blackwell Ultra GPU，以及最高 748GB 统一内存。 其中包括 252GB HBM3e GPU 内存和 496GB LPDDR5X CPU 内存，AI 算力最高可达 20 PFLOPS，支持运行参数规模最高约 1 万亿的模型。 与传统高性能工作站相比，DGX Station 的核心卖点在于将数据中心级硬件、统一内存和 NVIDIA AI 软件栈压缩到桌面设备中。开发者可以在本地进行模型微调、推理、智能体开发和生成式 AI 应用测试，减少数据上传云端带来的延迟、成本和隐私压力。 NVIDIA 官方还将 DGX Station 与 Windows 生态结合，意味着开发者可在熟悉的 Windows 环境中使用本地大模型能力，并探索 AI 智能体、Copilot 和混合智能应用。 其最高功耗达到 1,600W，并需要 20A 电路，显示出这款设备虽然采用桌面形态，但更接近一台面向专业用户的本地 AI 基础设施。

ab100df7ae079d32.title: 特朗普签署行政令把 AI 改叫 SI，推出美国政府对话式问答网站
ab100df7ae079d32.title_original: 特朗普签署行政令把 AI 改叫 SI，推出美国政府对话式问答网站
ab100df7ae079d32.summary: IT之家 9 月 30 日消息，美东时间周二（9 月 29 日），美国总统特朗普正式签署行政令，下令所有行政部门和机构 使用“超级智能”（Super Intelligence，简称 SI）一词代替人工智能（AI） 。 特朗普在行政令中表示：美国创新者开创的非凡技术远超“人工智能”一词初次出现时的设想。当今前沿系统的能力远不止模仿或自动化人类智能的离散方面。它们不断放大人类的创造力，解锁新的创造力形式，使美国人能够实现此前在科学、医学及几乎所有其他人类领域中不可能实现的目标。随着这些能力的不断提升， 它们越来越代表着不仅仅是人工智能，更是超级智能的新纪元 。 行政令还称，美国联邦政府使用的术语应反映这些技术的变革能力及其为美国人民创造的无限机遇。因此，“超级智能”一词更恰当地反映了这些技术的潜力、潜力和快速发展的能力。因此，特朗普政府的政策是，在法律允许的最大范围内，行政部门应使用“超级智能”和“SI”来替代“人工智能”和“AI”， 并且不会承认“人工智能”和“AI”在任何适用环境中的使用 。 IT之家注意到，特朗普当天还宣布推出了 America.gov ，这是一个为美国人在线访问联邦政府信息或服务的数字入口，他签署了一项行政令，确保美国联邦机构能够与 America.gov 整合。 现在， 美国人可以在 America.gov 上提出任何问题，并获得最新的答案 。今年晚些时候，美国人将能够在 America.gov 上完成护照续签和医疗保险注册等任务，而不必再被送回“一堆迷宫般的网站”。随着机构整合，更多服务将逐步部署到 America.gov 。

f206b7749ca4a813.summary: IT之家 9 月 30 日消息，在北京时间 9 月 30 日凌晨 1 点举行的 OpenAI DevDay 2026 活动中，OpenAI 宣布升级插件扩展。 借助插件扩展，开发者可以直接在 ChatGPT 中构建丰富的应用内体验。现在， 用户可以为插件在侧边栏中设置专属入口 ，构建可供用户一边对话一边工作的交互面板，或为产品支持的文件类型创建查看器。 此外，插件创建工具可以帮助开发者构建插件，重新设计的提交流程则提供更清晰的反馈。 OpenAI 还在改进插件目录和对话中的插件排序与推荐方式 ，帮助用户找到相关插件。用户始终可以自主选择使用哪些插件，并逐一批准其访问权限。 现在， 用户可以将受支持的 ChatGPT 插件接入自己构建的站点 ，让工作空间中的团队成员凭各自的权限登录同一应用，并使用各自连接的数据。OpenAI 还简化了自动化流程的添加和管理，让站点中的共享信息保持最新。（适用于 Business、Enterprise、医疗保健版和 Education 套餐） IT之家从发布会获悉，OpenAI 正在加入对拟议的 MCP 事件规范的支持， 让插件能够在已连接的应用中发生事件时启动自动化流程 。例如，用户可以让 ChatGPT 关注项目看板上的新任务。有新任务时，即使用户不在，ChatGPT 也能阅读关联文档并起草计划。
